question: What is the collective term for all the external structures of the female reproductive system?
explanation: The vulva is the medical term used to describe all the external female genital structures combined. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why must a nurse know the exact landmarks of the vulva?

options.A: To pass a urinary catheter without missing the urethra
options.D: To track the exact day of ovulation

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy keeps procedures safe and stops you from accidentally placing a catheter into the vaginal opening instead of the urethra.

question: Which layer of the uterus is primarily responsible for contractions during childbirth?
explanation: The myometrium is made of thick smooth muscle that contracts forcefully to push the baby out during labor. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of the rugae inside the vaginal canal?

options.B: To let the vagina stretch wide during childbirth
options.C: To trap bacteria and stop infections
options.D: To produce the monthly period blood

explanation: Well done! Those little folds (rugae) act like an accordion, giving extra tissue so the vagina can safely stretch during delivery.

question: Where does fertilization of an egg by a sperm normally happen?
explanation: Correct! The sperm and egg usually meet and fuse right there in the fallopian tube on their journey.

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To sweep over the ovary and catch the released egg
options.B: To push sperm upward into the uterine cavity
options.C: To attach the ovary firmly to the pelvic wall
options.D: To secrete hormones that trigger monthly ovulation

explanation: The finger-like fimbriae use gentle sweeping movements to guide the newly released egg into the fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers ovulation around day 14 of the cycle?
explanation: You nailed it! A sudden spike in luteinizing hormone (LH) is the green light that causes the ovary to release a mature egg.

question: What causes the uterine lining to shed at the start of a new menstrual cycle?

options.A: A sharp drop in estrogen and progesterone
options.B: A sudden spike in body temperature

explanation: That is correct! When pregnancy doesn't happen, hormone levels drop, telling the body it's time to shed the lining during menstruation.

question: What hormone directly stimulates the initial growth and maturation of ovarian follicles?
explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is released by the pituitary gland to stimulate ovarian follicles to grow. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h5)

question: What happens to the follicular cells left behind in the ovary after ovulation?

options.A: They turn into permanent scar tissue
options.B: They turn into the corpus luteum and make progesterone
options.C: They travel down to meet the egg
options.D: They immediately dissolve and leave the pelvis

explanation: Spot on! The empty follicle gets a makeover into the corpus luteum, pumping out progesterone to get the uterus ready for a possible pregnancy.

question: How is menopause officially diagnosed in a patient?

options.A: Surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.B: A sudden spike in body temperature
options.D: Twelve straight months without a menstrual period

explanation: You got it! Clinicians look back and confirm menopause once a woman has gone a full 12 months without any bleeding.

question: Why do women often lose bone density after reaching menopause?

options.A: High FSH destroys the bone marrow
options.B: Lower estrogen levels remove the protective effect on bones
options.D: Lack of progesterone stops water absorption

explanation: Correct! Estrogen helps keep bones strong, so when it drops after menopause, the risk of weak bones (osteoporosis) goes up.

question: What does the abbreviation LMP stand for in nursing assessments?
explanation: Easy and essential! LMP means Last Menstrual Period—a super important detail you will ask almost every female patient.

question: A patient comes to the clinic with severe lower belly pain and irregular bleeding. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Take a detailed menstrual history, including her last period date
options.C: Tell the patient menopause has started
options.D: Advise her to stop all physical activity

explanation: Brilliant! Always start with a thorough history. Knowing her menstrual pattern helps the team figure out what might be going wrong.
